name: Auris Spire Concert Hall
description:
Auris occupies floors 312 through 318 of the Helion Meridian Tower in Spire District 1, its main performance chamber a gravity-defying ellipsoid of acoustic metamaterial panels and suspended holographic projection arrays. Seating capacity is eight hundred in the primary chamber, with each seat equipped with a neural-sync interface offering individually calibrated sensory augmentation — patrons with chrome-enhanced hearing receive additional frequency layers composed specifically for augmented perception, while baseline listeners receive a curated mix optimized for unaugmented neurology. The effect is that two people seated side by side may experience the same performance in measurably different ways, both versions considered the definitive experience by their respective listeners.

Auris is operated by Vantablack Media's luxury events subsidiary, Aurelius Cultural Holdings, and a single ticket to a standard performance runs between Φ800 and Φ4,000 depending on augmentation tier and seat class. Private boxes with full neural-sync suites can be reserved for Φ40,000 per evening. The hall commissions and premieres original works by high-profile artists — recent seasons have featured Tarquin Osei-Mäkinen's Peregrine Suite performed live for the first time, and the world premiere of Spire Sequence No. 13 by the AI-human collaborative ensemble that performs under the name AXIOM//SLEEP. The building's exterior facade pulses with bioluminescent panels visible from the Circuit districts below on clear nights.
creator: Aurelius Cultural Holdings
genre: neural ambient, orchestral synthesis, augmented perception composition, AI-collaborative
audience: Tier 4 corporate professionals and Tier 5 elite, corporate clients entertaining guests, augmentation enthusiasts, AI music researchers
cultural_impact: Auris represents the apex of what GLMZ's establishment considers high culture, and its programming decisions function as a de facto canon-setting mechanism for what the corporate tier recognizes as serious music. Artists who premiere at Auris receive immediate legitimacy in Tier 4 and 5 markets, and the hall's rejection of an artist can suppress their Vantablack distribution access. Paradoxically, Auris has become an unlikely object of fascination for Shelf and Circuit musicians — not out of aspiration but out of contempt and curiosity in equal measure. Bootleg neural recordings of Auris performances, stripped of the official sensory layers and distributed on pirate feeds, are consumed widely in lower tiers as a kind of stolen luxury.
known_fans: pirate feed listeners who consume bootleg recordings ironically
story_hooks: A bootleg neural recording of an Auris premiere is circulating on the Shelf mesh — but it contains something in the sub-augmented frequency layers that was never meant to be heard outside the building, something that sounds like a confession.

A Tier 1 musician has been anonymously commissioned to compose a piece for an Auris premiere under a false identity — the hall's curators have no idea who they are actually platforming, and someone wants to keep it that way until the night of the performance.

Someone has sabotaged the neural-sync infrastructure of Auris's private boxes, and the next performance is in six hours — the question is whether the sabotage was meant to harm the audience, the performers, or simply to transmit something through eight hundred simultaneously connected minds.
